questions.question: To file nomination for the Presidential election, a signed list of _____ proposers is required.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**50**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 
__ 

• To file a nomination for the **Presidential election** in India, the candidate must have a list of **50 proposers** who are members of the **Electoral College**. This is a mandatory requirement under the Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, 1952. 

• In addition to the proposers, the candidate must also have **50 seconders**. Both proposers and seconders must be members of Parliament or State Legislative Assemblies. 

• The nomination form must be accompanied by a security deposit of **₹15,000** as per the rules set by the Election Commission of India. 

• The provision for 50 proposers and seconders was introduced to prevent frivolous nominations for the Presidential election and ensure the seriousness of the candidature. 

• The Electoral College for the Presidential election comprises elected members of the **Rajya Sabha**, **Lok Sabha**, and the **Legislative Assemblies** of states and Union Territories. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
__ 

• **Presidential Election Procedure:** 
 

• The **President of India** is elected by an Electoral College as per Article 55 of the **Constitution of India**. 

• The election follows the principle of **proportional representation** using the **single transferable vote system**. 

• The Electoral College includes elected members of both Houses of Parliament and elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of States and Union Territories. 

• Nominations are scrutinized by a Returning Officer appointed by the Election Commission of India. 
 
 

• **Eligibility Criteria for Presidential Candidates:** 
 

• A candidate must be a citizen of India. 

• The candidate must be at least **35 years old**. 

• The candidate must be qualified to become a member of the Lok Sabha. 

• The candidate cannot hold any office of profit under the Government of India or any state government. 
 
 

• **Security Deposit:** 
 

• A candidate filing a nomination must deposit an amount of **₹15,000**. 

• This deposit is forfeited if the candidate fails to secure one-sixth of the votes cast. 
 
 

• **Election Commission's Role:** 
 

• The **Election Commission of India** oversees the entire process of the Presidential election, including notifications, nominations, scrutiny, voting, and counting. 

• The Chief Election Commissioner acts as the Returning Officer for the election. 
 
 

• **Notable Facts:** 
 

• The first Presidential election in India was held in **1952**. 

• The current President of India is elected every **five years**, but a sitting President can be re-elected. 

• India’s first President was **Dr. Rajendra Prasad**, who served from 1950 to 1962. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
 

• **Role of Proposers and Seconders:** 
 

• Proposers and seconders play a crucial role in authenticating the candidature of an individual for the Presidential election. 

• They ensure the nomination process is not misused by individuals without serious intentions or proper qualifications. 

• Both proposers and seconders must sign the nomination papers of the candidate. 
 
 

• **Electoral College Details:** 
 

• The Electoral College includes members from the Union and State legislatures. 

• Nominated members of Parliament and State Assemblies are excluded from the Electoral College. 

• The votes are weighted based on the population of the states as per the 1971 Census. 
 
 

• **Voting Process:** 
 

• Voting is conducted through a secret ballot to ensure confidentiality. 

• Each voter uses a special pen to mark preferences on the ballot paper. 

• The counting process involves the calculation of quota based on valid votes, ensuring proportional representation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__
 
__ 

• **Lumbini** is the birthplace of **Lord Buddha**, the founder of Buddhism. It is located in the **Rupandehi District** of **present-day Nepal**. 

• Lumbini is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**, recognized for its cultural and historical significance. It was inscribed in the year **1997**. 

• The birthplace of Buddha in Lumbini is marked by the **Mayadevi Temple**, named after his mother, Queen Maya Devi. The site also features the **Ashokan Pillar**, erected by Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE. 

• The grove where Buddha was born is called the **Lumbini Garden**. It was a serene grove at the time and remains a significant pilgrimage site for Buddhists worldwide. 

• The archaeological remains at Lumbini include monasteries, stupas, and inscriptions, which provide crucial insights into the historical and religious importance of the site. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
__ 

• **Buddha's Birth:** 
 

• Lord Buddha, originally named **Siddhartha Gautama**, was born in **Lumbini** in **563 BCE**. He belonged to the **Shakya clan**, and his father was King **Suddhodana**. 

• Buddha’s birth in Lumbini is said to have occurred under a **sal tree** in the garden, where Queen Maya Devi stopped during her journey to her parental home. 

• The **UNESCO inscription** emphasizes the spiritual message of peace and enlightenment associated with the site. 
 
 

• **Significance of Lumbini:** 
 

• Lumbini is one of the **four major pilgrimage sites** for Buddhists, along with **Bodh Gaya** (enlightenment), **Sarnath** (first sermon), and **Kushinagar** (parinirvana). 

• The **Mayadevi Temple** is considered the main attraction, housing a marker stone that signifies the exact spot of Buddha's birth. 

• The site contains ancient ruins and monasteries from the **3rd century BCE** to the **9th century CE**, making it an important archaeological and spiritual center. 

• Visitors often light lamps and offer prayers at the temple, symbolizing peace and enlightenment. 
 
 

• **Other Options:** 
 

• **Pavapuri:** Located in Bihar, India, it is associated with **Jainism** and is the place where Lord Mahavira, the 24th Tirthankara, attained nirvana. It is not related to Lord Buddha. 

• **Ujjain:** A city in Madhya Pradesh, India, known for its **Mahakaleshwar Temple** and significance in Hinduism. It has no connection with Buddha's birth. 

• **Kushinagar:** Located in Uttar Pradesh, India, this is the place where Buddha attained **parinirvana** (final enlightenment) after his death. It is an important Buddhist site but not his birthplace. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
 

• **The Ashokan Pillar:** 
 

• The Ashokan Pillar at Lumbini carries an inscription in **Brahmi script**, commemorating Emperor Ashoka’s visit to the site in the **3rd century BCE**. 

• The inscription is one of the oldest references to Lumbini as Buddha's birthplace. 
 
 

• **UNESCO Recognition:** 
 

• The **Lumbini Development Trust** was established to preserve and develop the site as a center for global peace and learning. 

• The site attracts pilgrims and tourists from across the world, promoting the message of harmony and enlightenment.

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 

__ 
 
• The **Seventh Schedule** of the **Indian Constitution** contains three lists: the Union List, the State List, and the Concurrent List. 
 
• These lists define the distribution of powers and functions between the **Union Government** and **State Governments**. 
 
• The **Union List** includes subjects of national importance such as defense, foreign affairs, banking, and atomic energy, which are under the exclusive legislative jurisdiction of the Parliament. 
 
• The **State List** includes subjects of local or state-level importance such as police, public health, and agriculture, which are under the exclusive legislative jurisdiction of State Legislatures. 
 
• The **Concurrent List** includes subjects such as education, marriage, and adoption, where both the Union and State Governments can make laws. However, in case of a conflict, the law made by the Parliament prevails. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 

__ 
 
• **Sixth Schedule:** 
 
 
• The **Sixth Schedule** pertains to the administration of tribal areas in the states of **Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram**. 
 
• It provides for the formation of **Autonomous District Councils** and Regional Councils to safeguard the rights of indigenous communities. 
 
• These councils have legislative, administrative, and judicial powers in specified areas under their jurisdiction. 
 
 
 
• **Eighth Schedule:** 
 
 
• The **Eighth Schedule** lists the **official languages** recognized by the Constitution of India. 
 
• Currently, the schedule includes **22 languages**, such as Hindi, Bengali, Tamil, Telugu, and Urdu. 
 
• The schedule aims to preserve and promote regional languages and cultural diversity in India. 
 
 
 
• **Fifth Schedule:** 
 
 
• The **Fifth Schedule** deals with the administration and control of **Scheduled Areas** and **Scheduled Tribes** in various states except for those in the Sixth Schedule. 
 
• It contains provisions for the establishment of **Tribal Advisory Councils** and the declaration of Scheduled Areas. 
 
• The President is empowered to declare certain areas as Scheduled Areas under this schedule. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 

 
 
• The **Seventh Schedule** is crucial for maintaining the federal structure of India by clearly demarcating the legislative authority of the Union and State Governments. 
 
• The Constitution also provides a mechanism for resolving disputes between the Union and States in cases of overlapping jurisdiction through the **Concurrent List**. 
 
• Amendments to the Seventh Schedule require the approval of both the Parliament and a majority of state legislatures under Article 368, emphasizing the importance of cooperative federalism. 
 
• The lists in the Seventh Schedule can be restructured or updated through constitutional amendments to address emerging needs and challenges faced by the nation.

__ 

• The campaign "**TB will lose, the country will win**" was launched by the **Indian Government** in alignment with its ambitious goal of eliminating **Tuberculosis (TB) by 2025**. 

• This target is **five years ahead** of the globally set Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) timeline, which aims to eradicate TB by **2030**. 

• The campaign was launched under the umbrella of the **National Strategic Plan for Tuberculosis Elimination (2017–2025)**, which is being spearheaded by the **Ministry of Health and Family Welfare**, Government of India. 

• It emphasizes enhanced **detection, treatment, and prevention** of TB cases and focuses on a patient-centric approach by involving communities and local health systems. 

• The campaign also includes leveraging advanced diagnostic tools like **CBNAAT (Cartridge Based Nucleic Acid Amplification Test)** and treatment options such as **Bedaquiline and Delamanid** for drug-resistant TB cases. 

• India shoulders the **highest burden** of TB in the world, with the campaign aiming to significantly reduce **incidence, prevalence, and mortality rates** caused by TB in the country.

__ 

• **About Tuberculosis (TB):** 
 

• TB is a contagious airborne disease caused by the bacterium **Mycobacterium tuberculosis**. 

• It primarily affects the lungs (Pulmonary TB) but can also impact other organs (Extrapulmonary TB). 

• Symptoms include **chronic cough, fever, weight loss, and night sweats**. 

• Drug-resistant TB (MDR-TB and XDR-TB) poses a major challenge to global health systems. 
 
 

• **National Tuberculosis Elimination Program (NTEP):** 
 

• Formerly known as the Revised National Tuberculosis Control Program (RNTCP), it is India's flagship program for TB control. 

• The program provides **free diagnostic and treatment services** to TB patients across the country. 

• It utilizes **DOTS (Directly Observed Treatment, Short-course)** strategy to ensure treatment adherence.

• Approximately **10.6 million people** fell ill with TB globally in **2021**.

• **CBNAAT and TrueNat:** Rapid molecular tests for detecting TB and resistance to Rifampicin (a key TB drug).

• **Community Participation:** 
 

• India's TB elimination strategy emphasizes the involvement of **NGOs, local bodies, and community health workers**. 

• Initiatives like **TB Champions**, where cured patients advocate for TB awareness and early diagnosis, are critical.

• **Article 62** of the **Constitution of India** belongs to **Part V**, which deals with the Union Government, including the **Executive, Legislature, and Judiciary**.

• **Article 62** specifically deals with provisions for filling a vacancy in the office of the **President of India** and the related timeline for conducting elections. 
 
• It states that if the office of the President becomes vacant due to death, resignation, removal, or otherwise, the election to fill the vacancy must be held within **six months**. 
 
• It ensures continuity in the functioning of the Union Government and avoids any constitutional crisis. **Hence, Article 62 is correctly associated with Part V.**

• **Article 79:** Defines the composition of the Parliament of India, including the President, Lok Sabha, and Rajya Sabha.

• Acts as a safeguard against political or administrative instability at the Union level.

__ 

• **Kumaradevi**, the daughter of the chief of the **Lichchhavis**, was married to **Chandragupta I**, the first significant ruler of the **Gupta dynasty**. 

• The marriage between Chandragupta I and Kumaradevi was a strategic alliance that strengthened the Gupta dynasty's political power and influence in northern India. 

• This alliance with the Lichchhavis, a prominent republican clan, helped Chandragupta I gain legitimacy and expand his territories. 

• Chandragupta I declared himself the **Maharajadhiraja** (king of kings) after his marriage to Kumaradevi, marking the beginning of the Gupta Empire's golden age. 

• The Gupta dynasty is known for its contributions to art, culture, science, and literature, and this matrimonial alliance played a pivotal role in establishing its foundations. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
__ 

• **Chandragupta I:** 
 

• He ruled from approximately **320 CE to 335 CE**. 

• His reign marked the beginning of the **Gupta Era**, which is considered a golden age in Indian history due to advancements in various fields. 

• Chandragupta I's decision to form alliances through marriage, such as with the Lichchhavis, proved to be crucial in expanding the Gupta Empire's influence. 
 
 

• **The Lichchhavis:** 
 

• The Lichchhavis were a prominent republican clan from the region of **Vaishali** (in modern-day Bihar). 

• They had a significant influence in ancient Indian politics and were known for their democratic governance system. 

• Their alliance with the Guptas through Kumaradevi's marriage elevated the Gupta dynasty's status and power. 
 
 

• **Gupta Empire’s Contributions:** 
 

• The Gupta Empire is renowned for its advancements in fields such as **astronomy**, **mathematics** (e.g., Aryabhata's work), **literature** (e.g., Kalidasa's plays), and **art**. 

• It is often referred to as the **Golden Age of India**. 

• The empire extended across northern and central India, with its capital at **Pataliputra** (modern-day Patna). 
 
 

• **Role of Kumaradevi:** 
 

• Kumaradevi's marriage to Chandragupta I symbolized the union of two powerful dynasties, enhancing the political and cultural prestige of the Gupta dynasty. 

• Coins were issued during Chandragupta I's reign, depicting him and Kumaradevi together, signifying the importance of their union. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
 

• **Samudragupta:** 
 

• He was the son of Chandragupta I and Kumaradevi and succeeded his father as the ruler of the Gupta Empire. 

• Samudragupta is known as the **Napoleon of India** due to his military conquests and expansion of the empire. 
 
 

• **Chandragupta II:** 
 

• He was the son of Samudragupta and one of the most celebrated rulers of the Gupta dynasty. 

• His reign marked the zenith of the Gupta Empire's power and cultural achievements. 
 
 

• **Ghatotkacha:** 
 

• He was the father of Chandragupta I and an earlier ruler of the Gupta dynasty.

• The **Constitution (100th Amendment) Act, 2015** operationalized the **Indo-Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement (LBA)**, which was originally signed in **1974** and ratified in **2015**.
 
• This agreement aimed to resolve the long-pending issue of enclaves and adverse possessions along the **India-Bangladesh border**.
 
• It resulted in the exchange of **enclaves** between the two countries. India transferred 111 enclaves measuring **17,160 acres** to Bangladesh, while Bangladesh transferred 51 enclaves covering **7,110 acres** to India.
 
• Approximately **14,000 residents** of these enclaves were given the option to choose their citizenship, thereby addressing the statelessness of these populations.
 
• The amendment altered the **First Schedule** of the Indian Constitution, which specifies the territorial extent of each Indian state, particularly affecting the borders of **Assam, West Bengal, Meghalaya, and Tripura**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indo-Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement (LBA):**
 
 
• The agreement aimed to resolve disputes and uncertainty concerning enclaves and adverse possessions between the two nations.
 
• It was signed during the tenure of Indian Prime Minister **Indira Gandhi** and Bangladeshi President **Sheikh Mujibur Rahman** in **1974**, but the formal exchange of enclaves was completed in **2015**.
 
• The implementation required a constitutional amendment, specifically the **100th Amendment Act**, to adjust India's territorial extent as defined in the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the 100th Amendment Act:**
 
 
• It enhanced bilateral relations between India and Bangladesh by addressing a longstanding boundary issue.
 
• The exchange of enclaves resolved the issue of **stateless citizens**, providing them with clarity on their nationality.
 
• It facilitated the development and integration of these areas into the respective countries' administrative and socio-economic frameworks.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of the Amendment:**
 
 
• The First Schedule of the Constitution was amended to modify the territorial boundaries of **Assam, West Bengal, Meghalaya, and Tripura**.
 
• The amendment ensured that the transfer of enclaves was carried out in accordance with the principles of the Constitution and international law.
 
 
 
• **Other Related Amendments:**
 
 
• **The Constitution (98th Amendment) Act, 2012:** This amendment dealt with the establishment of a new bench of the **Gauhati High Court** for Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• **The Constitution (99th Amendment) Act, 2014:** This amendment dealt with the establishment of the **National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC)**, which was later struck down by the Supreme Court.
 
• **The Constitution (101st Amendment) Act, 2016:** This amendment introduced the **Goods and Services Tax (GST)** in India, creating a unified indirect taxation system.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of the 100th Amendment:**
 
 
• It addressed one of the oldest border disputes in South Asia and fostered peace and cooperation between India and Bangladesh.
 
• The amendment was a significant step in resolving humanitarian issues faced by the residents of the exchanged enclaves.

__ 

• A **tissue** is a group of cells that have a similar structure and work together to perform a specific function. This is the correct definition of a tissue. 

• Tissues are classified into four basic types in animals: **epithelial tissue, connective tissue, muscle tissue,** and **nervous tissue**. Each type has specialized roles. 

• In plants, tissues are broadly categorized into **meristematic tissue** (involved in growth) and **permanent tissue** (for functions like transport and support). 

• Proteins, enzymes, and organs are not a group of cells but instead have distinct roles in biological systems. Hence, these options are incorrect. 

• The **structure and function of tissues** vary depending on their location and role in the organism. For example, muscle tissue in animals is specialized for movement, while xylem tissue in plants is adapted for water transport. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
 

• **Protein:** 
 

• Proteins are large, complex molecules composed of one or more chains of amino acids. 

• They perform a variety of functions, including **enzymatic activity, structural support, signaling, and transport**. Examples include hemoglobin and insulin. 

• Proteins are not made up of cells but are synthesized within cells, typically in the ribosomes. 
 
 

• **Enzyme:** 
 

• Enzymes are biological molecules, usually proteins, that act as **catalysts** to speed up chemical reactions in the body. 

• They are highly specific to the reactions they catalyze and are not composed of cells. 

• Examples include **amylase** (breaks down starch) and **lipase** (breaks down fats). 
 
 

• **Organ:** 
 

• An organ is a group of tissues that work together to perform a specific function in the body. For example, the heart is an organ that pumps blood. 

• Organs are made up of multiple types of tissues, not just one specific type of cell. 

• Examples of organs include the **lungs, liver, heart, and brain**. 
 
 

• **Tissues in Plants:** 
 

• Plant tissues are categorized into **meristematic** (for growth) and **permanent tissues** (for support, transport, and other functions). 

• Examples include **xylem** (water transportation) and **phloem** (transport of nutrients). 
 
 

• **Tissues in Animals:** 
 

• Animal tissues are categorized into four types: **epithelial, connective, muscle,** and **nervous tissues**. 

• Each tissue type has a specialized function: epithelial tissue covers surfaces, connective tissue provides support, muscle tissue enables movement, and nervous tissue processes signals.

• The Sarnath pillar is particularly famous as it bears the **Lion Capital of Ashoka**, which was later adopted as the National Emblem of India. 
 
• This pillar was erected by **Emperor Ashoka** in the 3rd century BCE, commemorating the site where Buddha delivered his first sermon, known as the **Dharmachakra Pravartana (Turning of the Wheel of Dharma)**.

• The pillar’s **easternmost location** among Mauryan pillars signifies Ashoka's dedication to spreading his policies and Buddhist teachings across a vast region. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 

__ 
 
• **Mauryan Pillars:** 
 
• The Mauryan pillars were built during the reign of Emperor Ashoka (268-232 BCE) as a part of his efforts to disseminate his edicts and Buddhist philosophy. 
 
• These pillars are made of **polished sandstone** and are remarkable for their intricate carvings and inscriptions. 
 
• Most of these pillars have inscriptions in the **Brahmi script** and are written in the **Prakrit language**. 
 
 

 
• **Sarnath Lion Capital:** 
 
• The Lion Capital at Sarnath consists of four lions standing back-to-back, symbolizing **power, courage, and confidence**. 
 
• It is mounted on a circular abacus, adorned with carvings of animals like elephants, horses, bulls, and lions, representing the four cardinal directions. 
 
• The abacus also features the **Dharmachakra (Wheel of Dharma)**, signifying the universal spread of Buddhist teachings.

• **Topra:** Originally located in Haryana, the Topra pillar is another Ashokan pillar later moved to Feroz Shah Kotla in Delhi by Sultan Feroz Shah Tughlaq. 
 
• **Meerut:** The Ashokan pillar at Meerut, Uttar Pradesh, is another example of the Mauryan architecture, showcasing Ashoka's inscriptions. 
 
 

 
• **Emperor Ashoka:** 
 
• He was a significant ruler of the Mauryan Empire, known for his conversion to Buddhism after the **Kalinga War**. 
 
• Ashoka’s reign is marked by the spread of Buddhist teachings across the Indian subcontinent and beyond to regions like Sri Lanka, Central Asia, and Southeast Asia.

• **Architectural Features of Mauryan Pillars:** 
 
• The pillars are typically monolithic, with a tapering shaft topped by a capital (often with animal sculptures). 
 
• They are made of **Chunar sandstone**, known for its fine finish and polish. 
 
• The inscriptions reflect Ashoka’s **Dhamma policy**, emphasizing non-violence, tolerance, and welfare for all. 
 
 

 
• **Significance of the Pillars:**

• The pillars highlight the **advanced craftsmanship** and engineering skills of the Mauryan period.

questions.question: Which of the following services provides the facility for holding shares and securities in an electronic format?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Demat account**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 
__ 
 
• A **Demat account** is a facility that allows investors to hold **shares and securities electronically**, eliminating the need for physical certificates. 
 
• It was introduced in **India** under the **Depositories Act, 1996** to streamline the process of buying, selling, and transferring securities. 
 
• Demat accounts are maintained by **depositories** such as **National Securities Depository Limited (NSDL)** and **Central Depository Services Limited (CDSL)**, with brokers acting as intermediaries. 
 
• It offers benefits like **easy transfer of securities**, **reduction in paperwork**, and **elimination of risks** such as theft or damage associated with physical share certificates. 
 
• Opening a Demat account is mandatory for trading in **stock markets** in India, as per guidelines set by the **Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)**. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
__ 
 
• **Special Deposit Schemes:** 
 
 
• These schemes are typically designed to cater to specific needs such as housing or pension funds. 
 
• They do not provide facilities to hold shares or securities electronically. 
 
• Examples include fixed deposits or recurring deposit schemes offered by banks. 
 
 
 
• **Current Account:** 
 
 
• Primarily used by businesses and companies for **frequent transactions**. 
 
• It does not deal with the holding of shares or securities. 
 
• Features include **overdraft facility** and no limit on the number of transactions. 
 
 
 
• **Savings Account:** 
 
 
• A savings account is designed for individuals to **save money** and earn interest. 
 
• It does not offer facilities to hold shares or securities electronically. 
 
• Typically used for **personal banking needs** like deposits and withdrawals. 
 
 
 
• **Functionality of Demat Accounts:** 
 
 
• Demat accounts allow investors to **trade in stock markets**, mutual funds, exchange-traded funds (ETFs), and bonds. 
 
• Investors can convert their **physical certificates into electronic format** through a process called dematerialization. 
 
• It simplifies record-keeping and ensures **transparency** in transactions. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
 
 
• **Mandatory Requirement:** 
 
 
• As per **SEBI guidelines**, having a Demat account is mandatory for trading in the Indian stock market. 
 
 
 
• **Depository Participants (DPs):** 
 
 
• Brokers act as intermediaries between investors and depositories like **NSDL** or **CDSL**. 
 
 
 
• **Security Features:** 
 
 
• Demat accounts provide **secure storage** for securities, reducing risks like loss, theft, or forgery. 
 
 
 
• **Global Comparison:** 
 
 
• Similar systems exist globally, such as the **Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC)** in the United States.

• The flag consisted of three colors: green, saffron, and red, symbolizing **freedom, strength, and courage**, respectively. It also included symbols like the lotus and the sun, representing India’s rich cultural heritage and bright future. 

• Her action aimed to draw global attention to India’s struggle for independence from British colonial rule and to seek international support for the cause. 

• Madam Cama’s act is considered a **pioneering moment in India’s freedom struggle**, symbolizing courage and determination against colonial oppression.</l
